title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named Coral Gables campus places for collaborative work, focused research, creative projects, and outdoor breaks.

cards.title: Otto G. Richter Library
cards.subtitle: Central library on the Coral Gables campus
cards.notes: Start at the central library when your plan needs research help, technology, collections, or a place to settle into academic work.
cards.short_summary: A central academic hub with study support, collections, and technology-rich services.
cards.evidence_claim: Richter Library is UM's central interdisciplinary library and provides the university community with study support, a Learning Commons, Creative Studio, and research services.
cards.access_notes: Check the library's current hours and access guidance before visiting.

cards.title: Learning Commons at Richter
cards.subtitle: First floor, Otto G. Richter Library
cards.notes: Use this first-floor hub to reserve a study space, find course materials, or connect with academic support services.
cards.short_summary: A shared first-floor academic-services space inside Richter Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Learning Commons is on Richter Library's first floor and offers study-space reservations, equipment access, course materials, and academic-service connections.
cards.access_notes: Services and space availability can vary; use the library's reservation and appointment links as needed.

cards.title: Creative Studio
cards.subtitle: Otto G. Richter Library
cards.notes: Bring a digital project and use the studio’s available Mac or Windows workstation when its specialized software fits your work.
cards.short_summary: A library workspace equipped for digital media and software-based projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Richter's Creative Studio has Mac workstations and a Dell Windows computer, with priority for people needing the installed software or hardware.
cards.source_title: Creative Studio at Richter Library: Computers
cards.access_notes: Computer use is subject to studio policies and priority for specialized software or hardware needs.

cards.title: Richter Stack Tower
cards.subtitle: Floors 4–9, Otto G. Richter Library
cards.notes: Choose the tower when you need quiet individual study, and keep conversations and phone use low to respect the designated zone.
cards.short_summary: Upper library floors designated for quiet, individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Richter's Stack Tower floors 4, 5, 6, 7, and 9 are designated for quiet, individual study.
cards.access_notes: Keep phones on silent or vibrate and limit conversations in the quiet zone.

cards.entity_name: Kislak Center at the University of Miami
cards.title: Kislak Center
cards.subtitle: Ground floor, Otto G. Richter Library
cards.notes: Visit the gallery or plan a research session in the reading room when a primary-source project calls for special collections.
cards.short_summary: A special-collections center with exhibitions and a reading room for research.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kislak Center is on the ground floor of Richter Library, houses Special Collections and University Archives, and includes a gallery and reading room.
cards.access_notes: Research access and handling requirements may apply; review collection guidance before a materials visit.

cards.title: Cuban Heritage Collection Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Roberto C. Goizueta Pavilion, Richter Library
cards.notes: Book ahead when your work needs Cuban or diaspora primary sources, then request the materials you want to consult on site.
cards.short_summary: An appointment-based reading room for Cuban and diaspora research materials.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cuban Heritage Collection Reading Room is open for in-person research Monday through Friday by advance booking and seat reservation.
cards.access_notes: Advance booking, seat reservation, and requested materials are required; review the collection's appointment instructions.

cards.title: Architecture Research Center
cards.subtitle: University of Miami School of Architecture
cards.notes: Use the ARC for architecture, urban-planning, and design research; reserve a study room or computer station when your project needs one.
cards.short_summary: A subject library for architecture and urban planning and design research.
cards.evidence_claim: The Architecture Research Center holds a core architecture and urban-planning-and-design collection and offers study-room booking and public computer stations.
cards.access_notes: Visitor access, hours, and study-room reservations are governed by ARC policies; verify them before arrival.

cards.entity_name: Marta and Austin Weeks Music Library
cards.title: Weeks Music Library
cards.subtitle: University of Miami Coral Gables campus
cards.notes: Head here for music-focused work, then use the designated quiet areas or group rooms according to the library’s study-zone guidance.
cards.short_summary: A music library with designated quiet-study areas and group-study exceptions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Weeks Music Library's first-floor Listening Lab and second floor are quiet-study zones, except for group study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Keep phones on silent or vibrate and limit conversations in designated quiet areas.

cards.title: Gifford Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Coral Gables campus landscape collection
cards.notes: Take a short outdoor reset while observing the labeled plant collection, or use the site as a starting point for plant-focused coursework.
cards.short_summary: A campus arboretum used for education and research as well as tropical-plant appreciation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gifford Arboretum contains more than 650 trees and shrubs representing more than 500 species and is maintained for education and research.
cards.source_title: University of Miami Tree Care Plan
cards.access_notes: Use established campus paths and respect plantings, classes, and research activity.

cards.title: Butterfly Gardens
cards.subtitle: Along the Ibis Walking Trail near Gifford Arboretum
cards.notes: Walk the Ibis trail behind Eaton Residential College and pause at the garden to observe its plantings and visiting butterflies.
cards.short_summary: A campus living-laboratory garden along the Ibis Walking Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The Butterfly Gardens are along the Ibis Walking Trail behind Eaton Residential College, next to the Gifford Arboretum, and serve as living laboratories.
cards.source_title: University of Miami Tree Care Plan
cards.access_notes: Stay on established paths and avoid disturbing plants, insects, or any teaching and research activity.
